evidence: Approvals are posted only by post_verdict (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:745 post_approve_review) and the id is persisted in the very next statement (752); the Action engine posts approvals as github-actions[bot], a different actor the App-scoped sweeps never target (tools/pr-approval-agent/github.py:93-95), so 'hosted/local engine posting directly' is not a source of App approvals without an id. The only GitHub-only approval source is a crash between 745 and 752. Temporal retries post_verdict (constants.py:66-76: 3 attempts, 5s/10s, 5-min start_to_close on a dead worker); a same-head retry adopts the orphan via list_own_active_approvals (activities.py:726-752), so that case is closed. Residual hole: if the head moves before the retry, the retry marks the run SUPERSEDED and calls _dismiss_orphaned_approval (676-685), which no-ops on posted_review_id None (599), returns skipped_head_moved, and the workflow completes normally, so neither mark_review_failed (820) nor the terminal GitHub-side sweep (808/857) runs. The push's synchronize then either enters the workflow, whose startup dismiss_stale_approvals runs the GitHub-side own-approvals sweep with keep=empty (266-300, closes it), or lands on a skip path (tasks.py:894 opt-out/untrusted, 930 disabled, 951 label-absent, 983 author-below-write), all of which call _retract_stale_approvals_on_skip (483-517) -> dismiss_stale_approvals_for_head, which is DB-keyed on posted_review_id__isnull=False (logic/approvals.py:49-52) and cannot see the orphan; skip paths also never supersede the run. The activity docstrings themselves state the DB sweep is blind to GitHub-only approvals and add the GitHub sweep for that reason (activities.py:293-296, 513-515), while _retract_stale_approvals_on_skip's docstring (483-492) claims parity with the workflow's dismissal but mirrors only the DB half. Existing skip-path tests patch the helper and never seed a GitHub-only approval (tests/test_tasks.py:231-275, 826). The claim is real but the finding overstates it: it needs a hard crash inside a sub-second window (or a DB write failure right after a successful GitHub POST), a push before the retry (5s-5min), and that push routed to a skip path; it is not attacker-drivable and the codebase already closes the same-head and main-path variants.
notes: I would upgrade to should_fix if the head-moved retry path (activities.py:676-685) were shown to run on a routine cadence (e.g. worker SIGKILL during rollouts) or if a skip route were common after an approval (LABEL mode keeps the label on APPROVE, so label_absent needs a manual label removal). I would downgrade to not-real if the skip paths superseded the run or if any skip path already called _sweep_own_github_approvals, or if a same-head adopt provably always beats a push (it does not: retry waits 5s-5min).
